target: Cargo documented failure-closed use-time dependency resolution when local dependency material is already available
action: Inspected exactly the official Cargo Book cargo-build and cargo-fetch command documentation for --offline, --locked, and --frozen semantics, using only current open_source LATEST as role-local semantic context. No Cargo command, dependency repository, build, or runtime execution was performed.

public_sources.title: cargo build - The Cargo Book
public_sources.evidence: The command documentation states that --offline prevents Cargo from accessing the network for any reason; --locked requires the existing lockfile and exact dependency resolution or exits with an error; --frozen is equivalent to --locked plus --offline.

public_sources.title: cargo fetch - The Cargo Book
public_sources.evidence: The command documentation states that with Cargo.lock, cargo fetch makes git/registry dependencies locally available for subsequent offline Cargo commands until the lockfile changes; --offline forbids network access; --locked errors when the lockfile is missing or would change; --frozen combines both.

finding: At documentation level, Cargo provides a fail-closed use-time guard: --offline forbids network access, and --frozen simultaneously forbids network access and forbids lockfile drift. Therefore, when the exact local dependency material and lockfile already exist, a Cargo build/fetch path can be configured so that unmet remote needs cannot silently fall back to network access; the command must remain offline, and lockfile mismatch is an error. This is use-time dependency-resolution evidence only, not proof that the required local material can itself be created without a residual richer-mode or user-execution step.
scope_guard: This checkpoint establishes only current official documentation semantics for Cargo build/fetch flags and the relationship between a previously fetched local dependency set and later offline commands. It does not establish successful execution for any concrete project, completeness of a particular Cargo.lock, checksum correctness, local source integrity, initial vendor/cache population without network, compilation, runtime behavior, or end-to-end richer-mode parity.

hard_gate_assessment.use_time_network_fallback: documentation-level eliminated by --offline; --frozen additionally locks resolution
